Package frc.robot.utils.targeting

Class ShotPlanner

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.utils.targeting.ShotPlanner
public final class ShotPlanner extends Object
Turns the robot's pose and velocity into a turret angle and a shot. Pure math, so it can be tested on the desktop: no motors, NetworkTables or clocks.

Steps

  1. Project the robot pose (position and heading) forward by the latency, to where it will be when the ball leaves.
  2. Place the turret pivot on the projected pose and measure the displacement to the target.
  3. Scale that displacement by the radial (toward/away) latency term.
  4. Solve for the flight time tau with tau = TOF(|d - v * tau|) (Newton's method), where v is the pivot's field velocity: the ball inherits it, so aiming at the target shifted by -v * tau cancels the drift.
  5. Take the hood/RPM from the solver at that virtual distance, and the turret angle from the bearing to the virtual target and the projected heading.

    • plan

      public static ShotPlanner.ShotPlan plan(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose2d pose, edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.ChassisSpeeds fieldSpeeds, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d pivotOffset, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation3d target, ShotSolver solver, double latencyS, double rangeLatencyS)
      Parameters:
      pose - current robot pose
      fieldSpeeds - robot velocity, field-relative
      pivotOffset - turret pivot position in the robot frame (meters)
      target - target position on the field, or null for no target
      solver - shot solver, or null for none
      latencyS - how far ahead to project the pose (seconds)
      rangeLatencyS - extra projection applied only along the line to the target (seconds)
